operations.text: 0.3.20 narrows the red-then-green rule. In review.md, section Test quality, red-then-green proof is now owed only for a new test, or a test whose assertion the ticket changed, that asserts a behavior the ticket adds or changes. The unit of proof is the fault, not the test: one named fault, one red run, and the hand-back names the tests that went red under it; a failure before a test's own assertion proves nothing for that test, and a test written before the production change whose failing run against the old behavior is in the hand-back already has its proof. Any other new or changed test is checked by reading. A missing red record is a note; it is a blocker only when the Reviewer names the fault under which the test stays green. A brief, a plan's verify line or a ticket's acceptance criterion may not widen the rule (ticket.md, section Ticket brief contract; the planner brief). The Writer agent's VERIFY and Done contract, the Writer line of ticket.md section Role boundaries and work.md section Tests say the same. This update re-renders work.md, ticket.md, review.md and the Writer agent, each additions block carried. If your project carries a local rule that keeps every red run as a file, asks for a red run per new or changed test, or blocks on a missing red record alone, that rule now contradicts review.md section Test quality: delete or narrow it on the operator's word.
